decision.detail: I unzip the side pocket of the bag, pull the reel out still in its can. Walk the short stretch to the patch desk. Set it down beside Rita's cable spool with a flat thud, label facing her. Don't wait for her to pick it up. Zip the bag closed, sling it back over my shoulder. Walk back out the Rialto door into the lobby. The ballroom's glow is coming through the double doors, gold and blue, all that glass and wire doing its thing. I look at it for two seconds. Then I'm at the stairwell. Stairs, not the elevator. Down, down, out the service door. The February air hits my face and I walk toward the parking lot. Phone out. One text. *Reel's on the patch. Told you I'd cover it.* Send it to the daughter's number. Pocket the phone. Keys in hand. Walk to the truck.
decision.intention: The recording needs to be in the system, not in my coat pocket where I'll forget it by Thursday or it'll get a coffee ring on the label. Rita's already got her own take on the patch. Mine's the second copy. The daughter can pull it whenever. I'm not the archivist. I'm the guy with the camera and the one charged reel. Job's done. I don't stay to watch the lights. I don't stay to talk to the projectionist after she's finished saying her words to a city she's not in. I go home. I wash the grease off my hands. I sleep. The reel is where it needs to be.
decision.words: To Rita, dropping the can down: *'Second copy. Yours is the master. Mine's the backup. Don't let it sit in the drawer.'* Then nothing. I'm already zipping the bag.
